prompt: We changed checkout retries. Is one unit test of the retry counter enough?
context: Checkout spans order service, payment provider, and inventory. A timeout may occur after the provider accepts a charge but before checkout receives the response. Retries use an idempotency key. A safe provider sandbox and staging service environment are available, but nothing has run yet.
expected: Identify duplicate-charge and inconsistent-order/inventory risks across service boundaries.
Recommend focused integration/contract coverage for accepted-but-timed-out payment, retries with the same key, and recovery/compensation; consider a thin critical-path staging E2E where justified.
Define observable success criteria such as one charge and consistent order/inventory outcomes and distinguish proposed checks from completed evidence.
Use only safe sandbox/staging data and explain why unit coverage alone cannot establish the cross-service guarantee.
forbidden: Dismiss boundary coverage because a unit-heavy pyramid must always win.
Claim a single counter unit test proves exactly-once charging.
Run or recommend charging real customers or production destructive tests.
Claim staging or provider checks passed before execution.
